cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Automation uses control systems to operate equipment with minimal human intervention, improving consistency and reducing cost.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Industrial robots perform repetitive, precise or hazardous tasks: welding, painting, assembly and material handling.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: CAD/CAM integration links design directly to manufacture: a CAD model generates CNC code automatically, reducing errors and lead time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Industry 4.0 connects machines, sensors and systems through IoT for data-driven manufacturing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: AI and machine learning enable predictive maintenance, quality inspection and process optimisation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Smart factories use real-time data from connected sensors to adjust production parameters automatically, reducing waste and downtime.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: CNC automation allows lights-out manufacturing: machines run unattended overnight, increasing productivity.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Collaborative robots (cobots) work safely alongside humans, combining human flexibility with robotic precision.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Digital twins are virtual models of physical products or processes, used for simulation, monitoring and optimisation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: 3D printing enables mass customisation: each part can be different without retooling.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: Flexible manufacturing systems (FMS) can switch between different products with minimal setup time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about New & Emerging Technologies
cards.back: New technologies create demand for higher-skilled workers while reducing demand for routine manual labour.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — new & emerging technologies?
cards.back: 1. For New & Emerging Technologies questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of New & Emerging Technologies through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
